name: CubeSat Structure
description: A basic frame for mounting and protecting spacecraft hardware.
whyItMatters: The structure supports every part and adds mass even though it does not generate science.

name: Compact Deployable Solar Array
description: A compact deployable panel set that converts sunlight into power.
whyItMatters: This light array suits modest payloads, but power margin becomes tight with several instruments.

name: High-Efficiency Solar Array
description: A larger, more efficient panel set for higher-power missions.
whyItMatters: It buys power margin for ambitious payloads, with a higher price and mass penalty.

name: Lithium-Ion Battery Pack
description: Stores energy for eclipse and peak power use.
whyItMatters: The spacecraft must store enough energy to keep operating while it passes through Earth's shadow.

name: Extended-Capacity Battery
description: A larger energy store for long eclipses and high-power payloads.
whyItMatters: Extra stored energy helps during long shadows but adds mass and launch cost.

name: Radiation-Tolerant Flight Computer
description: A flight computer designed to better withstand radiation upsets.
whyItMatters: Hardening costs more, but reduces the chance that radiation interrupts your mission.

name: Basic Flight Computer
description: A lightweight computer that runs spacecraft commands.
whyItMatters: It saves cost and mass, but is less protected in harsh radiation environments.

name: Precision Pointing System
description: Reaction wheels and sensors keep the spacecraft accurately aimed.
whyItMatters: High-resolution imagers and telescopes need a steady, accurately pointed platform.

name: Basic Attitude Control
description: A basic system for orienting the spacecraft.
whyItMatters: It is enough for broad measurements, but less precise than a reaction-wheel system.

name: Cold-Gas Propulsion
description: A simple thruster system for small orbit adjustments.
whyItMatters: Propellant can extend useful life or enable maneuvers, but both the tank and fuel take payload mass.

name: Chemical Transfer Stage
description: A compact chemical stage with a heavier tank and high-thrust engine.
whyItMatters: It can provide the large maneuver budget needed for lunar capture, but fuel and tank mass consume launch capacity.

name: Low-Gain Antenna
description: A simple antenna with modest data capacity.
whyItMatters: It is lightweight and inexpensive, but can leave a data backlog if instruments collect data quickly.

name: Medium-Gain Antenna
description: A steerable antenna balancing mass, data rate, and pointing needs.
whyItMatters: It returns several times more data than a low-gain antenna without the full mass and power cost of a deep-space dish.

name: High-Gain Antenna
description: A directional antenna for fast, long-distance data return.
whyItMatters: More downlink capacity returns more science, but a directional antenna needs power and careful pointing.

name: Deep-Space High-Gain Antenna
description: A high-gain dish and transmitter tuned for very long communication distances.
whyItMatters: It can close a deep-space link, but distance still limits the rate and precise pointing is important.

name: Solid-State Data Recorder
description: Stores science data until a ground station contact is available.
whyItMatters: A larger buffer gives the spacecraft time to wait for a ground pass before data must be discarded.
